claim: HGF/Met signaling has recently been associated with basal-type breast cancers.
source: HGF/Met signaling has recently been associated with basal-type breast cancers, which are thought to originate from progenitor cells residing in the luminal compartment of the mammary epithelium.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established association, without specific data provided in this manuscript.

claim: Basal-type breast cancers are thought to originate from progenitor cells residing in the luminal compartment of the mammary epithelium.
source: HGF/Met signaling has recently been associated with basal-type breast cancers, which are thought to originate from progenitor cells residing in the luminal compartment of the mammary epithelium.
evidence: This represents current scientific understanding cited in the abstract.

claim: ICAM-1 efficiently marks mammary luminal progenitors comprising hormone receptor-positive and receptor-negative cells.
source: We found that ICAM-1 efficiently marks mammary luminal progenitors comprising hormone receptor-positive and receptor-negative cells, presumably ductal and alveolar progenitors.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data and gene expression analysis shown in Figures 1 and 8.

claim: ICAM-1-positive luminal progenitors include presumably ductal and alveolar progenitors.
source: We found that ICAM-1 efficiently marks mammary luminal progenitors comprising hormone receptor-positive and receptor-negative cells, presumably ductal and alveolar progenitors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the hormone receptor status and developmental timing of the populations.

claim: Both hormone receptor-positive and receptor-negative luminal progenitor populations strongly express Met.
source: Both cell populations strongly express Met, while HGF is produced by stromal and basal myoepithelial cells.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figures 2A and 8D.

claim: HGF is produced by stromal cells.
source: Both cell populations strongly express Met, while HGF is produced by stromal and basal myoepithelial cells.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: HGF is produced by basal myoepithelial cells.
source: Both cell populations strongly express Met, while HGF is produced by stromal and basal myoepithelial cells.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figures 2A and 2B.

claim: Persistent HGF treatment stimulates the clonogenic activity of ICAM1-positive luminal progenitors.
source: We show that persistent HGF treatment stimulates the clonogenic activity of ICAM1-positive luminal progenitors, controlling their survival and proliferation, and leads to the expression of basal cell characteristics, including stem cell potential.
evidence: This is supported by colony formation assays and sphere culture data shown in Figures 2C-F.

claim: HGF treatment controls survival of ICAM1-positive luminal progenitors.
source: We show that persistent HGF treatment stimulates the clonogenic activity of ICAM1-positive luminal progenitors, controlling their survival and proliferation, and leads to the expression of basal cell characteristics, including stem cell potential.
evidence: This is supported by caspase activity assays shown in Figure 2E.

claim: HGF treatment controls proliferation of ICAM1-positive luminal progenitors.
source: We show that persistent HGF treatment stimulates the clonogenic activity of ICAM1-positive luminal progenitors, controlling their survival and proliferation, and leads to the expression of basal cell characteristics, including stem cell potential.
evidence: This is supported by BrdU incorporation assays shown in Figure 2F.

claim: HGF treatment leads to the expression of basal cell characteristics in luminal progenitors.
source: We show that persistent HGF treatment stimulates the clonogenic activity of ICAM1-positive luminal progenitors, controlling their survival and proliferation, and leads to the expression of basal cell characteristics, including stem cell potential.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence and qPCR data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: HGF treatment leads to stem cell potential in luminal progenitors.
source: We show that persistent HGF treatment stimulates the clonogenic activity of ICAM1-positive luminal progenitors, controlling their survival and proliferation, and leads to the expression of basal cell characteristics, including stem cell potential.
evidence: This is supported by transplantation assays shown in Figure 7.

claim: HGF treatment induces Snai1 expression in luminal progenitors.
source: This is accompanied by the induction of Snai1 and Snai2, two major transcription factors triggering epithelial–mesenchymal transition, the repression of the luminal-regulatory genes Elf5 and Hey1, and claudin down-regulation.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: HGF treatment induces Snai2 expression in luminal progenitors.
source: This is accompanied by the induction of Snai1 and Snai2, two major transcription factors triggering epithelial–mesenchymal transition, the repression of the luminal-regulatory genes Elf5 and Hey1, and claudin down-regulation.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR and immunofluorescence data shown in Figures 4B and 4D.

claim: Snai1 and Snai2 are major transcription factors triggering epithelial–mesenchymal transition.
source: This is accompanied by the induction of Snai1 and Snai2, two major transcription factors triggering epithelial–mesenchymal transition, the repression of the luminal-regulatory genes Elf5 and Hey1, and claudin down-regulation.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge cited in the manuscript.

claim: HGF treatment represses Elf5 expression in luminal progenitors.
source: This is accompanied by the induction of Snai1 and Snai2, two major transcription factors triggering epithelial–mesenchymal transition, the repression of the luminal-regulatory genes Elf5 and Hey1, and claudin down-regulation.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: HGF treatment represses Hey1 expression in luminal progenitors.
source: This is accompanied by the induction of Snai1 and Snai2, two major transcription factors triggering epithelial–mesenchymal transition, the repression of the luminal-regulatory genes Elf5 and Hey1, and claudin down-regulation.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Elf5 is a luminal-regulatory gene.
source: This is accompanied by the induction of Snai1 and Snai2, two major transcription factors triggering epithelial–mesenchymal transition, the repression of the luminal-regulatory genes Elf5 and Hey1, and claudin down-regulation.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge cited in the manuscript.

claim: Hey1 is a luminal-regulatory gene.
source: This is accompanied by the induction of Snai1 and Snai2, two major transcription factors triggering epithelial–mesenchymal transition, the repression of the luminal-regulatory genes Elf5 and Hey1, and claudin down-regulation.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge cited in the manuscript.

claim: HGF treatment leads to claudin down-regulation in luminal progenitors.
source: This is accompanied by the induction of Snai1 and Snai2, two major transcription factors triggering epithelial–mesenchymal transition, the repression of the luminal-regulatory genes Elf5 and Hey1, and claudin down-regulation.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR and immunofluorescence data shown in Figures 4B and 5C.

claim: Paracrine Met signaling can control the function of luminal progenitors during mammary development.
source: Our data strongly indicate that paracrine Met signaling can control the function of luminal progenitors and modulate their fate during mammary development and tumorigenesis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing HGF effects on luminal progenitors.

claim: Paracrine Met signaling can modulate the fate of luminal progenitors during mammary development.
source: Our data strongly indicate that paracrine Met signaling can control the function of luminal progenitors and modulate their fate during mammary development and tumorigenesis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing HGF-induced changes in cell fate markers.

claim: Paracrine Met signaling can control the function of luminal progenitors during tumorigenesis.
source: Our data strongly indicate that paracrine Met signaling can control the function of luminal progenitors and modulate their fate during mammary development and tumorigenesis.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental findings and known associations with cancer.

claim: Paracrine Met signaling can modulate the fate of luminal progenitors during tumorigenesis.
source: Our data strongly indicate that paracrine Met signaling can control the function of luminal progenitors and modulate their fate during mammary development and tumorigenesis.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental findings and known associations with cancer.

claim: The postnatal development of the mammary gland comprises growth and branching of epithelial ducts during puberty.
source: The postnatal development of the mammary gland comprises two distinct morphogenetic events: the growth and branching of epithelial ducts during puberty and the lobulo–alveolar development during pregnancy.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about mammary gland development.

claim: The postnatal development of the mammary gland comprises lobulo–alveolar development during pregnancy.
source: The postnatal development of the mammary gland comprises two distinct morphogenetic events: the growth and branching of epithelial ducts during puberty and the lobulo–alveolar development during pregnancy.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about mammary gland development.

claim: The mammary epithelium is embedded in a fatty connective tissue.
source: The mammary epithelium is embedded in a fatty connective tissue and organized as a bilayer, with a basal layer of myoepithelial cells and a luminal epithelial layer.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about mammary gland structure.

claim: The mammary epithelium is organized as a bilayer with a basal layer of myoepithelial cells and a luminal epithelial layer.
source: The mammary epithelium is embedded in a fatty connective tissue and organized as a bilayer, with a basal layer of myoepithelial cells and a luminal epithelial layer.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about mammary gland structure.

claim: During lactation, luminal cells produce milk.
source: During lactation, the luminal cells produce milk, whereas myoepithelial cells serve for milk expulsion.
evidence: This is established knowledge about mammary gland function.

claim: During lactation, myoepithelial cells serve for milk expulsion.
source: During lactation, the luminal cells produce milk, whereas myoepithelial cells serve for milk expulsion.
evidence: This is established knowledge about mammary gland function.

claim: The luminal cell layer is characterized by the expression of keratins 8/18/19.
source: The luminal cell layer is characterized by the expression of keratins 8/18/19 and comprises a subset of hormone-sensing cells that express estrogen, progesterone, and prolactin receptors (ER, PR, and PrlR, respectively) (Brisken, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Brisken, 2013.

claim: The luminal cell layer comprises a subset of hormone-sensing cells that express estrogen, progesterone, and prolactin receptors.
source: The luminal cell layer is characterized by the expression of keratins 8/18/19 and comprises a subset of hormone-sensing cells that express estrogen, progesterone, and prolactin receptors (ER, PR, and PrlR, respectively) (Brisken, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Brisken, 2013.

claim: Basal myoepithelial cells express keratins 5 and 14.
source: Basal myoepithelial cells express keratins 5 and 14, P-cadherin, the transcription factor p63, and smooth muscle-specific contractile proteins (Moumen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Moumen et al., 2011.

claim: Basal myoepithelial cells express P-cadherin.
source: Basal myoepithelial cells express keratins 5 and 14, P-cadherin, the transcription factor p63, and smooth muscle-specific contractile proteins (Moumen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Moumen et al., 2011.

claim: Basal myoepithelial cells express the transcription factor p63.
source: Basal myoepithelial cells express keratins 5 and 14, P-cadherin, the transcription factor p63, and smooth muscle-specific contractile proteins (Moumen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Moumen et al., 2011.

claim: Basal myoepithelial cells express smooth muscle-specific contractile proteins.
source: Basal myoepithelial cells express keratins 5 and 14, P-cadherin, the transcription factor p63, and smooth muscle-specific contractile proteins (Moumen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Moumen et al., 2011.

claim: The basal compartment specifically displays Slug/Snail2.
source: This compartment specifically displays Slug/Snail2 (Guo et al., 2012; Nassour et al., 2012), a key transcription factor coordinating the epithelial–mesenchymal (EMT) transition program (Thiery et al., 2009; Nieto and Cano, 2012; Gonzalez and Medici, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Guo et al., 2012 and Nassour et al., 2012.

claim: Slug/Snail2 is a key transcription factor coordinating the epithelial–mesenchymal transition program.
source: This compartment specifically displays Slug/Snail2 (Guo et al., 2012; Nassour et al., 2012), a key transcription factor coordinating the epithelial–mesenchymal (EMT) transition program (Thiery et al., 2009; Nieto and Cano, 2012; Gonzalez and Medici, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: The adult mammary basal compartment harbors multipotent stem cells able to fully regenerate the gland upon transplantation.
source: The adult mammary basal compartment harbors multipotent stem cells able to fully regenerate the gland upon transplantation (Shackleton et al., 2006; Stingl et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Shackleton et al., 2006 and Stingl et al., 2006.

claim: The luminal cell layer contains clonogenic cells, the luminal progenitors.
source: The luminal cell layer contains clonogenic cells, the luminal progenitors (Asselin-Labat et al., 2007; Sleeman et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Asselin-Labat et al., 2007 and Sleeman et al., 2007.

claim: The luminal progenitor population is heterogeneous, consisting of hormone receptor-positive and hormone receptor-negative clonogenic cells.
source: This population is heterogeneous, consisting of hormone receptor-positive and hormone receptor-negative clonogenic cells that are considered to be functionally distinct ductal and alveolar progenitors (Beleut et al., 2010; Regan et al., 2012; Shehata et al., 2012; Fu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: Hormone receptor-positive and hormone receptor-negative clonogenic cells are considered to be functionally distinct ductal and alveolar progenitors.
source: This population is heterogeneous, consisting of hormone receptor-positive and hormone receptor-negative clonogenic cells that are considered to be functionally distinct ductal and alveolar progenitors (Beleut et al., 2010; Regan et al., 2012; Shehata et al., 2012; Fu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: Luminal progenitors are able to drive the expansion of the luminal cell population in mammary ducts and alveoli during postnatal development.
source: According to lineage-tracing studies, these cells are able to drive the expansion of the luminal cell population in mammary ducts and alveoli during postnatal development (Van Keymeulen et al., 2011; Fu et al., 2014; Rios et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from lineage-tracing studies.

claim: Luminal progenitors are thought to be at the origin of triple-negative, basal-like, Brca1-associated breast cancers.
source: Moreover, luminal progenitors are thought to be at the origin of the triple-negative, basal-like, Brca1-associated breast cancers, indicating that they display phenotypic plasticity and an ability to upregulate basal markers (Lim et al., 2009; Molyneux et al., 2010; Proia et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: Luminal progenitors display phenotypic plasticity and an ability to upregulate basal markers.
source: Moreover, luminal progenitors are thought to be at the origin of the triple-negative, basal-like, Brca1-associated breast cancers, indicating that they display phenotypic plasticity and an ability to upregulate basal markers (Lim et al., 2009; Molyneux et al., 2010; Proia et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an inference from the cited studies about cancer origins.

claim: Ectopic expression of Snail2 endows luminal progenitors with basal cell features.
source: Of note, ectopic expression of Snail2 endows luminal progenitors with basal cell features (Guo et al., 2012), supporting an important role of EMT in the regulation of luminal progenitor plasticity.
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Guo et al., 2012.

claim: EMT plays an important role in the regulation of luminal progenitor plasticity.
source: Of note, ectopic expression of Snail2 endows luminal progenitors with basal cell features (Guo et al., 2012), supporting an important role of EMT in the regulation of luminal progenitor plasticity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited study showing Snail2 effects.

claim: The Met tyrosine kinase receptor and its major ligand, HGF, are known to control numerous epithelial cell functions and trigger EMT.
source: The Met tyrosine kinase receptor and its major ligand, HGF, are known to control numerous epithelial cell functions and trigger EMT (Trusolino et al., 2010; Gherardi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Trusolino et al., 2010 and Gherardi et al., 2012.

claim: Met signaling has been implicated in mammary development and tumorigenesis.
source: Met signaling has been implicated in mammary development and tumorigenesis.
evidence: This is established knowledge that is further elaborated in subsequent sentences.

claim: Met-deficient mammary glands of adult MMTV-Cre:Metf/f mice showed defects in branching morphogenesis.
source: Although not investigated in detail yet, Met-deficient mammary glands of adult MMTV-Cre:Metf/f mice showed defects in branching morphogenesis (Garner et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Garner et al., 2011.

claim: Aberrant Met activation occurs in breast cancers, in particular in the triple-negative, basal-like subtype.
source: Aberrant Met activation occurs in breast cancers, in particular in the triple-negative, basal-like subtype (Gastaldi et al., 2010; Ponzo and Park, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Gastaldi et al., 2010 and Ponzo and Park, 2010.

claim: Expression of activated Met or over-expression of HGF in mouse mammary gland induce tumors, including those of the basal-like subtype.
source: Expression of activated Met or over-expression of HGF in mouse mammary gland induce tumors, including those of the basal-like subtype (Graveel et al., 2009; Ponzo et al., 2009; Holland et al., 2013; Knight et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: In vitro studies have implicated HGF/Met signaling in the regulation of mammary epithelial cell growth, morphogenesis, and differentiation.
source: Several in vitro studies performed with mammary organoids or immortalized cell lines have implicated HGF/Met signaling in the regulation of mammary epithelial cell growth, morphogenesis, and differentiation (Soriano et al., 1995; Yang et al., 1995; Haslam et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: Luminal progenitors express Met and, when forced to express HGF, display an enhanced in vivo regenerative potential.
source: One recent work indicated that luminal progenitors express Met and that, when forced to express HGF, display an enhanced in vivo regenerative potential, a property attributed to basal-type stem cells (Gastaldi et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Gastaldi et al., 2013.

claim: Enhanced in vivo regenerative potential is a property attributed to basal-type stem cells.
source: One recent work indicated that luminal progenitors express Met and that, when forced to express HGF, display an enhanced in vivo regenerative potential, a property attributed to basal-type stem cells (Gastaldi et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Gastaldi et al., 2013.

claim: In situ, mammary luminal cells do not express HGF.
source: However, in situ, mammary luminal cells do not express HGF, suggesting that Met signaling in mammary epithelial cells is activated in a paracrine manner.
evidence: This is an observation that leads to the inference about paracrine signaling.

claim: Met signaling in mammary epithelial cells is activated in a paracrine manner.
source: However, in situ, mammary luminal cells do not express HGF, suggesting that Met signaling in mammary epithelial cells is activated in a paracrine manner.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that luminal cells do not express HGF.

claim: HGF-mediated paracrine and autocrine Met stimulation can trigger distinct biological responses in epithelial cells.
source: HGF-mediated paracrine and autocrine Met stimulation can trigger distinct biological responses in epithelial cells (Mai et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Mai et al., 2014.

claim: Met activation requires adhesion molecules as co-receptors.
source: Met activation requires adhesion molecules as co-receptors.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Met signaling.

claim: CD44v6 is a co-receptor for Met in hepatocytes.
source: Two co-receptors for Met have been identified in hepatocytes: CD44v6, the CD44 isoform containing the exon v6 and ICAM-1 (CD54), a member of the immunoglobulin superfamily of cell adhesion molecules (Orian-Rousseau et al., 2002; Olaku et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Orian-Rousseau et al., 2002 and Olaku et al., 2011.

claim: ICAM-1 is a co-receptor for Met in hepatocytes.
source: Two co-receptors for Met have been identified in hepatocytes: CD44v6, the CD44 isoform containing the exon v6 and ICAM-1 (CD54), a member of the immunoglobulin superfamily of cell adhesion molecules (Orian-Rousseau et al., 2002; Olaku et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Orian-Rousseau et al., 2002 and Olaku et al., 2011.

claim: ICAM-1 is a member of the immunoglobulin superfamily of cell adhesion molecules.
source: Two co-receptors for Met have been identified in hepatocytes: CD44v6, the CD44 isoform containing the exon v6 and ICAM-1 (CD54), a member of the immunoglobulin superfamily of cell adhesion molecules (Orian-Rousseau et al., 2002; Olaku et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ICAM-1.

claim: From puberty to late gestation, ICAM-1 is differentially expressed in the mammary epithelium.
source: From puberty to late gestation, ICAM-1 was differentially expressed in the mammary epithelium.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: ICAM-1 staining identifies three epithelial populations: negative, low-expressing, and high-expressing.
source: Staining for this marker identified three epithelial populations, negative (ICAM1-neg) or displaying low (ICAM1-low) or high (ICAM1-hi) levels of expression (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: At all stages of development, K5-expressing basal myoepithelial cells are located in the ICAM1-hi population.
source: Gene expression analysis by qPCR showed that, at all stages of development, K5-expressing basal myoepithelial cells were located in the ICAM1-hi population, while K8-positive luminal cells were distributed in ICAM1-neg and ICAM1-low-cell subsets (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: K8-positive luminal cells are distributed in ICAM1-neg and ICAM1-low-cell subsets.
source: Gene expression analysis by qPCR showed that, at all stages of development, K5-expressing basal myoepithelial cells were located in the ICAM1-hi population, while K8-positive luminal cells were distributed in ICAM1-neg and ICAM1-low-cell subsets (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: ICAM-1 can be used to identify the basal cell compartment and separate two populations of luminal cells.
source: Thus, ICAM-1 can be used to identify the basal cell compartment, and separate two populations of luminal cells, referred to hereafter as Lu-pos and Lu-neg cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the qPCR and flow cytometry data.

claim: In mature virgin mice and early in pregnancy, almost all the colony-forming activity is associated with the Lu-pos cell subset.
source: In adult virgin mice, almost all the colony-forming activity was associated with the Lu-pos cell subset, demonstrating that ICAM-1 expression delineates a luminal population highly enriched in clonogenic progenitors (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by colony formation assays shown in Figure 1C.

claim: ICAM-1 expression delineates a luminal population highly enriched in clonogenic progenitors.
source: In adult virgin mice, almost all the colony-forming activity was associated with the Lu-pos cell subset, demonstrating that ICAM-1 expression delineates a luminal population highly enriched in clonogenic progenitors (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the colony formation data.

claim: ICAM-1 efficiently marks mammary luminal progenitors from adult virgin Balb/c mice.
source: Notably, ICAM-1 efficiently marked mammary luminal progenitors from adult virgin Balb/c (Figure 1C), C57Bl/6J (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) and Blg-Cre; R26 mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B–E).
evidence: This is supported by colony formation data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: ICAM-1 efficiently marks mammary luminal progenitors from adult virgin C57Bl/6J mice.
source: Notably, ICAM-1 efficiently marked mammary luminal progenitors from adult virgin Balb/c (Figure 1C), C57Bl/6J (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) and Blg-Cre; R26 mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B–E).
evidence: This is supported by colony formation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: ICAM-1 efficiently marks mammary luminal progenitors from adult virgin Blg-Cre; R26 mice.
source: Notably, ICAM-1 efficiently marked mammary luminal progenitors from adult virgin Balb/c (Figure 1C), C57Bl/6J (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) and Blg-Cre; R26 mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B–E).
evidence: This is supported by colony formation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B–E.

claim: LacZ activity is undetectable in basal myoepithelial cells in the mammary gland of adult virgin Blg-Cre; R26 females.
source: As expected from previous findings (Selbert et al., 1998; Molyneux et al., 2010), LacZ activity, as assessed by X-gal staining, was undetectable in basal myoepithelial cells and present in a subset of luminal cells in the mammary gland of adult virgin Blg-Cre; R26 females (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by X-gal staining shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and cited from previous studies.

claim: LacZ activity is present in a subset of luminal cells in the mammary gland of adult virgin Blg-Cre; R26 females.
source: As expected from previous findings (Selbert et al., 1998; Molyneux et al., 2010), LacZ activity, as assessed by X-gal staining, was undetectable in basal myoepithelial cells and present in a subset of luminal cells in the mammary gland of adult virgin Blg-Cre; R26 females (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by X-gal staining shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and cited from previous studies.

claim: Blg drives recombination primarily in the luminal progenitor population identified by ICAM-1.
source: An analysis of Cre expression by qPCR indicated that Blg (β-Lactoglobulin) drove recombination primarily in the luminal progenitor population identified by ICAM-1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: 98% of the colonies formed by ICAM1-expressing Blg-Cre; R26 luminal cells are LacZ-positive.
source: Accordingly, 98% of the colonies formed by ICAM1-expressing Blg-Cre; R26 luminal cells were LacZ-positive (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is supported by X-gal staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E.

claim: The non-clonogenic Lu-neg population has high levels of transcripts for hormone receptors ERα, PR, and PrlR.
source: The non-clonogenic Lu-neg population had high level of transcripts for the hormone receptors, ERα, PR, and PrlR, and for genes encoding secreted hormonal mediators implicated in the control of mammary development such as amphiregulin (encoded by Areg), RankL (encoded by Tnfsf11) and Wnt4.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The non-clonogenic Lu-neg population has high levels of transcripts for genes encoding secreted hormonal mediators including amphiregulin, RankL, and Wnt4.
source: The non-clonogenic Lu-neg population had high level of transcripts for the hormone receptors, ERα, PR, and PrlR, and for genes encoding secreted hormonal mediators implicated in the control of mammary development such as amphiregulin (encoded by Areg), RankL (encoded by Tnfsf11) and Wnt4.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Amphiregulin, RankL, and Wnt4 are implicated in the control of mammary development.
source: The non-clonogenic Lu-neg population had high level of transcripts for the hormone receptors, ERα, PR, and PrlR, and for genes encoding secreted hormonal mediators implicated in the control of mammary development such as amphiregulin (encoded by Areg), RankL (encoded by Tnfsf11) and Wnt4.
evidence: This is established knowledge about mammary development.

claim: Areg, Tnfsf11, Wnt4, and Ly6a are characteristic of mature mammary luminal cells.
source: These genes, along with Ly6a (encoding Sca-1), are characteristic of mature mammary luminal cells (Mulac-Jericevic et al., 2003; Kendrick et al., 2008; Cai et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: The clonogenic Lu-pos population expresses Mki67 more strongly than the Lu-neg fraction.
source: The clonogenic Lu-pos population expressed Mki67, a marker of cell proliferation, more strongly than the Lu-neg fraction.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The clonogenic Lu-pos population exhibits high levels of expression for genes encoding essential regulators of mammary development including Elf5, Hey1, RANK, and R-spondin1.
source: It exhibited high levels of expression for genes encoding essential regulators of mammary development including Elf5, the Notch effector, Hey1, RANK (encoded by Tnfrsf11a), and the local mediator R-spondin1 (encoded by Rspo1) (Fata et al., 2000; Bouras et al., 2008; Oakes et al., 2008; Cai et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1D and cited from multiple sources.

claim: Lu-pos cells over-express Kit and Itga2, two markers previously used to obtain mammary cell populations enriched in luminal progenitors.
source: Lu-pos cells also over-expressed Kit and Itga2, two markers previously used to obtain mammary cell populations enriched in luminal progenitors (Regan et al., 2012; Shehata et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1D and cited from previous studies.

claim: Met transcript levels are five times higher in the Lu-pos population than in the Lu-neg cells in adult virgin mice.
source: In adult virgin mice, Met transcript levels were five and ten times higher in the Lu-pos population than in the Lu-neg and myoepithelial cells, respectively; Gab1, like Met, was strongly expressed only in the Lu-pos fraction (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Met transcript levels are ten times higher in the Lu-pos population than in myoepithelial cells in adult virgin mice.
source: In adult virgin mice, Met transcript levels were five and ten times higher in the Lu-pos population than in the Lu-neg and myoepithelial cells, respectively; Gab1, like Met, was strongly expressed only in the Lu-pos fraction (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Gab1 is strongly expressed only in the Lu-pos fraction in adult virgin mice.
source: In adult virgin mice, Met transcript levels were five and ten times higher in the Lu-pos population than in the Lu-neg and myoepithelial cells, respectively; Gab1, like Met, was strongly expressed only in the Lu-pos fraction (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In adult virgin females and during early pregnancy, the target cells for Met signaling mostly belong to the luminal progenitor-enriched population defined by ICAM-1 expression.
source: Thus, in adult virgin females and during early pregnancy, the target cells for Met signaling mostly belonged to the luminal progenitor-enriched population defined by ICAM-1 expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the Met expression data.

claim: HGF is strongly expressed in the CD24-negative Pdgfr-expressing stromal cell population.
source: As expected (Niranjan et al., 1995; Yang et al., 1995), HGF, the major Met ligand, was strongly expressed in the CD24-negative Pdgfr-expressing stromal cell population (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2B and cited from previous studies.

claim: HGF is expressed at high level in the mammary basal cell population of mature virgin and early pregnant mice.
source: In addition, HGF was expressed at high level in the mammary basal cell population of mature virgin and early pregnant mice (Figure 2A,B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), suggesting paracrine interactions between basal myoepithelial cells and luminal progenitors.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figures 2A, 2B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: HGF expression in basal cells suggests paracrine interactions between basal myoepithelial cells and luminal progenitors.
source: In addition, HGF was expressed at high level in the mammary basal cell population of mature virgin and early pregnant mice (Figure 2A,B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), suggesting paracrine interactions between basal myoepithelial cells and luminal progenitors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the HGF expression pattern.

claim: Most cells of both Lu-pos and Lu-neg populations are stained with anti-CD44v6 antibody.
source: Most cells of both populations were stained with the anti-CD44v6 antibody (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: CD44v6 is broadly expressed in the luminal compartment and cannot be used for the enrichment in Met-expressing progenitors.
source: Thus, CD44v6 is broadly expressed in the luminal compartment and cannot, therefore, be used for the enrichment in Met-expressing progenitors.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the CD44v6 staining data.

claim: HGF-treated Lu-pos cells form enlarged spheres after 10 days in culture.
source: We found that HGF-treated Lu-pos cells formed enlarged spheres after 10 days in culture (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by phase contrast images and size distribution data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: HGF-treated spheres have multiple lumens with an overall lumen space larger than that of untreated spheres.
source: These spheres had multiple lumens, with an overall lumen space larger than that of the untreated spheres (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by H&E staining shown in Figure 2C.

claim: HGF-treated cultures of purified Lu-pos cells contain twice as many spheres as non-stimulated cultures.
source: Quantitative analysis revealed that HGF-treated cultures of purified Lu-pos cells contained twice as many spheres as non-stimulated cultures (Figure 2D), suggesting a role for HGF in favoring cell survival and/or proliferation.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: HGF favors cell survival and/or proliferation of Lu-pos cells.
source: Quantitative analysis revealed that HGF-treated cultures of purified Lu-pos cells contained twice as many spheres as non-stimulated cultures (Figure 2D), suggesting a role for HGF in favoring cell survival and/or proliferation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the increased sphere number.

claim: HGF-treated cells have lower levels of activated caspase-3 and caspase-7 than untreated cells after 2 days in culture.
source: Measurements of caspase activity showed that HGF-treated cells had lower levels of activated caspase-3 and caspase-7 than untreated cells after 2 days in culture (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by caspase activity assay data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: HGF treatment increases cell proliferation of Lu-pos cells, particularly on day 2.
source: BrdU-incorporation assays performed after 1, 2, and 4 days in culture indicated that HGF treatment increased cell proliferation, particularly on day 2 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by BrdU incorporation data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: In 3D cultures, HGF stimulates the clonogenic activity of ICAM1-expressing luminal progenitors by promoting cell survival and proliferation early in culture.
source: Thus, in 3D cultures, HGF stimulated the clonogenic activity of ICAM1-expressing luminal progenitors, by promoting cell survival and proliferation early in culture.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the caspase and BrdU data.

claim: Mki67 is down-regulated in HGF-stimulated cultures of Lu-pos cells after 9-10 days.
source: Mki67 was down-regulated in HGF-stimulated cultures whereas Cdkn1a, which encodes p21, a negative regulator of the cell cycle (Abbas and Dutta, 2009), was upregulated by a factor of 2.5.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Cdkn1a is upregulated by a factor of 2.5 in HGF-stimulated cultures of Lu-pos cells after 9-10 days.
source: Mki67 was down-regulated in HGF-stimulated cultures whereas Cdkn1a, which encodes p21, a negative regulator of the cell cycle (Abbas and Dutta, 2009), was upregulated by a factor of 2.5.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: p21 is a negative regulator of the cell cycle.
source: Mki67 was down-regulated in HGF-stimulated cultures whereas Cdkn1a, which encodes p21, a negative regulator of the cell cycle (Abbas and Dutta, 2009), was upregulated by a factor of 2.5.
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Abbas and Dutta, 2009.

claim: Krt5 is clearly expressed in HGF-stimulated spheres but undetectable in untreated spheres.
source: The basal-specific keratin, Krt5, undetectable in untreated spheres, was clearly expressed in HGF-stimulated spheres, whereas no significant decrease was observed in expression of the luminal-specific keratin, Krt18.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: No significant decrease is observed in Krt18 expression in HGF-stimulated spheres.
source: The basal-specific keratin, Krt5, undetectable in untreated spheres, was clearly expressed in HGF-stimulated spheres, whereas no significant decrease was observed in expression of the luminal-specific keratin, Krt18.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In the long-term, HGF/Met signaling biases luminal progenitors toward a basal cell fate while attenuating cell cycle progression.
source: Thus, in the long-term, HGF/Met signaling biased luminal progenitors toward a basal cell fate while attenuating cell cycle progression.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the gene expression data.

claim: The percentages of K5-positive cells in spheres stimulated with HGF for 9-10 days are six times higher than that of untreated cultures.
source: Consistent with the q-PCR data, immunofluorescence labeling showed that the percentages of K5-positive cells in spheres stimulated with HGF for 9–10 days were six times higher that that of untreated cultures (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Numerous K5-expressing cells in HGF-treated spheres stain positive for K8.
source: Numerous K5-expressing cells stained positive for K8 (Figure 3B), and none contained the myoepithelial-specific protein α-SMA (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: K5-expressing cells in HGF-treated spheres do not contain α-SMA.
source: Numerous K5-expressing cells stained positive for K8 (Figure 3B), and none contained the myoepithelial-specific protein α-SMA (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence and qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: K5-expressing cells do not cycle following HGF stimulation.
source: Interestingly, BrdU incorporation assays showed that, unlike K5-negative luminal cells, K5-expressing cells did not cycle following HGF stimulation (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by BrdU incorporation data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Paracrine Met activation controls the survival and proliferation of ICAM1-expressing luminal progenitors and favors the acquisition of basal-specific keratin.
source: Thus, paracrine Met activation controls the survival and proliferation of ICAM1-expressing luminal progenitors and favors the acquisition of basal-specific keratin.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data.

claim: 85% of K5-positive cells in HGF-stimulated cultures of Blg-Cre; R26 Lu-pos cells express LacZ.
source: Notably, in HGF-stimulated cultures, 85% of the K5-positive cells expressed LacZ and were therefore of luminal origin (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by X-gal staining and quantification shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: K5-positive cells expressing LacZ in HGF-stimulated cultures are of luminal origin.
source: Notably, in HGF-stimulated cultures, 85% of the K5-positive cells expressed LacZ and were therefore of luminal origin (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an inference based on the LacZ expression driven by the luminal-specific Blg promoter.

claim: Control HGF-treated basal cells do not stain positive for X-gal.
source: Control HGF-treated basal cells did not stain positive for X-gal.
evidence: This is supported by X-gal staining shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Upon stimulation with HGF, the expression of Elf5, Hey1, and Gata3 is repressed in luminal progenitors.
source: Upon stimulation with HGF, the expression of essential regulators of the luminal cell fate such as Elf5, Hey1, and Gata3 was repressed, whereas that of several basal-specific genes increased markedly.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Upon stimulation with HGF, the expression of several basal-specific genes including Cdh3, Trp63, and Snai2 increases markedly in luminal progenitors.
source: Upon stimulation with HGF, the expression of essential regulators of the luminal cell fate such as Elf5, Hey1, and Gata3 was repressed, whereas that of several basal-specific genes increased markedly. These genes included Cdh3 (encoding P-cadherin), Trp63, and the EMT inducer Snai2.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Snai1, Sox9, and Cdh2 are upregulated upon HGF stimulation of luminal progenitors.
source: Other genes associated with EMT program—Snai1, Sox9, and Cdh2 (encoding N-cadherin)—were also upregulated.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: HGF-treated spheres contain numerous p63-positive cells, whereas untreated cells are negative for p63.
source: In agreement with gene expression data, immunodetection studies revealed that HGF-treated spheres contained numerous p63- and Snail2-positive cells, whereas untreated cells were negative for these basal-specific markers (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: HGF-treated spheres contain numerous Snail2-positive cells, whereas untreated cells are negative for Snail2.
source: In agreement with gene expression data, immunodetection studies revealed that HGF-treated spheres contained numerous p63- and Snail2-positive cells, whereas untreated cells were negative for these basal-specific markers (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Snai2 and Snai1 can directly repress the transcription of Cdh1 and claudins.
source: Snai2 and Snai1 can directly repress the transcription of Cdh1 (encoding E-cadherin) and claudins (reviewed in Thiery et al., 2009; Gonzalez and Medici, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from review articles.

claim: Cdh1 expression is not significantly reduced upon HGF treatment of luminal progenitors.
source: Noticeably, Cdh1 expression was not significantly reduced upon HGF treatment, whereas claudin-1 and claudin-3 transcript levels decreased strongly (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Claudin-1 and claudin-3 transcript levels decrease strongly upon HGF treatment of luminal progenitors.
source: Noticeably, Cdh1 expression was not significantly reduced upon HGF treatment, whereas claudin-1 and claudin-3 transcript levels decreased strongly (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: E-cadherin is present in the vast majority of cell–cell contacts in untreated and HGF-treated spheres.
source: Consistent with the q-PCR data, immunofluorescence staining revealed E-cadherin in the vast majority of cell–cell contacts in untreated and HGF-treated spheres (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Numerous Snail2-positive cells in HGF-stimulated spheres display E-cadherin at their surface.
source: Notably, numerous Snail2-positive cells present in the HGF-stimulated spheres displayed E-cadherin at their surface (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Claudin-1 distribution is more heterogeneous than that of E-cadherin and is clearly altered following HGF treatment.
source: Claudin-1 distribution was more heterogeneous than that of E-cadherin, but it was clearly altered following HGF treatment.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Untreated spheres contain a majority of cells with claudin-1 at their junctions.
source: Untreated spheres contained a majority of cells with claudin-1 at their junctions, whereas HGF-treated spheres displayed large cell areas lacking claudin-1 expression (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: HGF-treated spheres display large cell areas lacking claudin-1 expression.
source: Untreated spheres contained a majority of cells with claudin-1 at their junctions, whereas HGF-treated spheres displayed large cell areas lacking claudin-1 expression (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Persistent stimulation of Met signaling by exogenous HGF in luminal progenitors represses luminal-regulatory gene expression.
source: Thus, the persistent stimulation of Met signaling by exogenous HGF in luminal progenitors repressed luminal-regulatory gene expression, upregulated basal-specific markers, and triggered an EMT program, including Snai2 and Snai1 expression and decrease in claudin levels.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the gene expression and immunofluorescence data.

claim: Persistent stimulation of Met signaling by exogenous HGF in luminal progenitors upregulates basal-specific markers.
source: Thus, the persistent stimulation of Met signaling by exogenous HGF in luminal progenitors repressed luminal-regulatory gene expression, upregulated basal-specific markers, and triggered an EMT program, including Snai2 and Snai1 expression and decrease in claudin levels.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the gene expression and immunofluorescence data.

claim: Persistent stimulation of Met signaling by exogenous HGF in luminal progenitors triggers an EMT program.
source: Thus, the persistent stimulation of Met signaling by exogenous HGF in luminal progenitors repressed luminal-regulatory gene expression, upregulated basal-specific markers, and triggered an EMT program, including Snai2 and Snai1 expression and decrease in claudin levels.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the gene expression and immunofluorescence data.

claim: Both clonogenic activity and level of Krt5 expression are much lower in secondary mammospheres deprived of HGF.
source: Both clonogenic activity and level of expression of the basal-specific keratin Krt5 were much lower in secondary mammospheres deprived of HGF (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6A and 6B.

claim: Secondary mammospheres deprived of HGF contain less than 1% K5-positive cells, like untreated control cultures.
source: Consistently, immunofluorescence stainings revealed that, like untreated control cultures, secondary mammospheres deprived of HGF contained less than 1% K5-positive cells (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 6C and 6D.

claim: HGF-treated secondary mammospheres contain twice more K5-positive cells than HGF-treated primary spheres.
source: HGF-treated secondary mammospheres contained twice more K5-positive cells than HGF-treated primary spheres.
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: In HGF-treated secondary mammospheres, K5-expressing cells are derived from LacZ-positive luminal cells.
source: Experiments performed with mammary luminal progenitors purified from BlgCre; R26 mice confirmed that, in HGF-treated secondary mammospheres, K5-expressing cells were derived from LacZ-positive luminal cells (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by X-gal staining shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Trp63, Snai2, and Cdkn1a are upregulated only in HGF-treated secondary mammospheres.
source: Gene expression analysis showed that Trp63, Snai2, and Cdkn1a were upregulated whereas Hey1, Elf5, and Mki67 were down-regulated only in HGF-treated secondary mammospheres (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Hey1, Elf5, and Mki67 are down-regulated only in HGF-treated secondary mammospheres.
source: Gene expression analysis showed that Trp63, Snai2, and Cdkn1a were upregulated whereas Hey1, Elf5, and Mki67 were down-regulated only in HGF-treated secondary mammospheres (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Continuous activation of HGF/Met signaling is required to sustain the response of luminal progenitors in vitro.
source: Thus, the continuous activation of HGF/Met signaling is required to sustain the response of luminal progenitors in vitro and leads to the accumulation of cells with basal characteristics.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the secondary sphere experiments.

claim: Continuous activation of HGF/Met signaling leads to the accumulation of cells with basal characteristics.
source: Thus, the continuous activation of HGF/Met signaling is required to sustain the response of luminal progenitors in vitro and leads to the accumulation of cells with basal characteristics.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the secondary sphere experiments.

claim: Untreated cells isolated from primary spheres fail to repopulate the fat pad or give rise to very limited outgrowths.
source: Untreated cells isolated from primary spheres failed to repopulate the fat pad or gave rise to very limited outgrowths.
evidence: This is supported by transplantation data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: HGF-treated cultures form ductal-type outgrowths in seven of the eight transplanted fat pads.
source: In contrast, HGF-treated cultures formed ductal-type outgrowths in seven of the eight transplanted fat pads (Figure 7A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by transplantation data shown in Figure 7A and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Only HGF-treated secondary spheres are able to form outgrowths upon transplantation.
source: Strikingly, these transplantation assays showed that only HGF-treated spheres were able to form outgrowths (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by transplantation data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: 6-week-old outgrowths from HGF-treated spheres are composed of well-organized ducts and growing buds comprising K8-positive luminal cells and basally located α-SMA-expressing myoepithelial cells.
source: 6-week-old outgrowths were composed of well-organized ducts and growing buds comprising K8-positive luminal cells and basally located α-SMA-expressing myoepithelial cells (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7C and 7D.

claim: Paracrine Met activation induces multipotent stem cell properties in luminal progenitors.
source: These data demonstrate that paracrine Met activation induced multipotent stem cell properties in luminal progenitors.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the transplantation experiments showing regenerative capacity.

claim: Differential Sca-1 expression in the luminal compartment delineates populations enriched in hormone receptor-positive and hormone receptor-negative cells, both containing clonogenic progenitors.
source: Differential Sca-1 expression in the luminal compartment has been reported to delineate populations enriched in hormone receptor-positive and hormone receptor-negative cells, both containing clonogenic progenitors (Sleeman et al., 2007; Regan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Sleeman et al., 2007 and Regan et al., 2012.

claim: Combined with Sca-1, ICAM-1 discriminates four cell populations in the luminal compartment: Lu1, Lu2, Lu3, and Lu4.
source: In adult virgin mammary gland, ICAM-1 separated both Sca-1-positive and Sca-1-negative cell populations, revealing four cell subsets, Lu1 (ICAM1-neg/Sca-1-pos), Lu2 (ICAM1-pos/Sca-1-pos), Lu3 (ICAM1-neg/Sca-1-neg), and Lu4 (ICAM1-pos/Sca-1-neg) accounting for 39.8 ± 4.6%, 9.1 ± 1.4%, 15.0 ± 2.5%, and 25.4 ± 6.1% of the luminal compartment, respectively (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Lu1 is considered as non-clonogenic (<0.5% colony-forming cells).
source: Lu1 was considered as non-clonogenic (<0.5% colony-forming cells), Lu3 cells, negative for ICAM-1, were poorly clonogenic whereas both Lu2 and Lu4 cells, positive for ICAM-1, were highly clonogenic (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by colony formation data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Lu3 cells are poorly clonogenic.
source: Lu1 was considered as non-clonogenic (<0.5% colony-forming cells), Lu3 cells, negative for ICAM-1, were poorly clonogenic whereas both Lu2 and Lu4 cells, positive for ICAM-1, were highly clonogenic (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by colony formation data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Both Lu2 and Lu4 cells are highly clonogenic.
source: Lu1 was considered as non-clonogenic (<0.5% colony-forming cells), Lu3 cells, negative for ICAM-1, were poorly clonogenic whereas both Lu2 and Lu4 cells, positive for ICAM-1, were highly clonogenic (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by colony formation data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: All four luminal cell subsets express K8 and display similar high levels of Krt18 and very low levels of Krt14.
source: All four luminal cell subsets expressed K8 and displayed similar high levels of Krt18 and very low levels of the basal-specific gene Krt14 (Figure 8A, Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry and qPCR data shown in Figure 8A and Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Unsupervised hierarchical clustering divides the four luminal populations into two main branches, with Lu1, Lu2, and Lu3 clustering together.
source: Unsupervised hierarchical clustering divided the populations into two main branches (Figure 8C). Lu1, Lu2, and Lu3 clustered together, sharing strong expression of hormone receptors, ERa, PR, and PrlR.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Lu1, Lu2, and Lu3 share strong expression of hormone receptors ERα, PR, and PrlR.
source: Unsupervised hierarchical clustering divided the populations into two main branches (Figure 8C). Lu1, Lu2, and Lu3 clustered together, sharing strong expression of hormone receptors, ERa, PR, and PrlR.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Lu4 displays very low levels of hormone receptor transcripts.
source: The second branch contained only Lu4, which displayed very low levels of hormone receptor transcripts.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Only Lu4 expresses the milk protein β-casein.
source: Only Lu4, the major clonogenic subset devoid of HR-positive cells, expressed the milk protein β-casein (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Lu4 strongly expresses Elf5 and Tnfrsf11a, two crucial regulators of alveologenesis.
source: It also strongly expressed Elf5 and Tnfrsf11a, two crucial regulators of alveologenesis (Fata et al., 2000; Oakes et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 8C and cited from previous studies.

claim: Lu4 is absent at puberty and appears in the glands of sexually mature cycling females.
source: Interestingly, flow cytometry analysis on mammary epithelial cells isolated at different stages of development showed that Lu4 was absent at puberty; this subset appeared in the glands of sexually mature cycling females and displayed massive expansion early in pregnancy (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Lu4 displays massive expansion early in pregnancy.
source: Interestingly, flow cytometry analysis on mammary epithelial cells isolated at different stages of development showed that Lu4 was absent at puberty; this subset appeared in the glands of sexually mature cycling females and displayed massive expansion early in pregnancy (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Lu2 and Lu3 are detected at all stages of development.
source: By contrast, Lu2 and Lu3 were detected at all stages of development.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Met is strongly expressed in the clonogenic populations Lu2 and Lu4.
source: The q-PCR analysis showed that Met was strongly expressed in the clonogenic populations, Lu2 and Lu4 (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Lu2 and Lu4 respond similarly to HGF treatment in 3D cultures.
source: These populations responded similarly to HGF treatment in 3D cultures. On stimulation, both produced larger spheres, displaying an upregulation of basal-specific genes (Snai2, Trp63, and Cdh3) and a down-regulation of luminal-specific regulatory genes (Gata3, Elf5, and Hey1) (Figure 8E,F).
evidence: This is supported by phase contrast images and qPCR data shown in Figure 8E and 8F.

claim: On HGF stimulation, both Lu2 and Lu4 produce larger spheres.
source: These populations responded similarly to HGF treatment in 3D cultures. On stimulation, both produced larger spheres, displaying an upregulation of basal-specific genes (Snai2, Trp63, and Cdh3) and a down-regulation of luminal-specific regulatory genes (Gata3, Elf5, and Hey1) (Figure 8E,F).
evidence: This is supported by phase contrast images shown in Figure 8E.

claim: On HGF stimulation, both Lu2 and Lu4 display an upregulation of basal-specific genes Snai2, Trp63, and Cdh3.
source: These populations responded similarly to HGF treatment in 3D cultures. On stimulation, both produced larger spheres, displaying an upregulation of basal-specific genes (Snai2, Trp63, and Cdh3) and a down-regulation of luminal-specific regulatory genes (Gata3, Elf5, and Hey1) (Figure 8E,F).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8F.

claim: On HGF stimulation, both Lu2 and Lu4 display a down-regulation of luminal-specific regulatory genes Gata3, Elf5, and Hey1.
source: These populations responded similarly to HGF treatment in 3D cultures. On stimulation, both produced larger spheres, displaying an upregulation of basal-specific genes (Snai2, Trp63, and Cdh3) and a down-regulation of luminal-specific regulatory genes (Gata3, Elf5, and Hey1) (Figure 8E,F).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8F.

claim: Luminal progenitors defined by ICAM-1 expression include hormone receptor-positive and hormone receptor-negative cells, all of which are potential targets of HGF/Met signaling.
source: These data show that luminal progenitors defined by ICAM-1 expression include hormone receptor-positive and hormone receptor-negative cells, all of which are potential targets of HGF/Met signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the characterization of Lu2 and Lu4 populations.

claim: In the pubertal gland, basal myoepithelial rather than luminal cells express ICAM-1.
source: Immunohistochemical studies confirmed that in the pubertal gland, basal myoepithelial rather than luminal cells expressed ICAM-1 while at late pregnancy, the whole epithelium was positive (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: At late pregnancy, the whole mammary epithelium is positive for ICAM-1.
source: Immunohistochemical studies confirmed that in the pubertal gland, basal myoepithelial rather than luminal cells expressed ICAM-1 while at late pregnancy, the whole epithelium was positive (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: At the onset of lactation, ICAM-1 is down-regulated both in ducts and alveoli.
source: At the onset of lactation, ICAM-1 was down-regulated both in ducts and alveoli (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: In adult virgin mice, mammary basal cells display high levels of ICAM-1.
source: In agreement with the flow cytometry data, mammary basal cells in adult virgin mice displayed high levels of ICAM-1, whereas the luminal compartment comprised ICAM1-negative and ICAM1-positive cells (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: In adult virgin mice, the luminal compartment comprises ICAM1-negative and ICAM1-positive cells.
source: In agreement with the flow cytometry data, mammary basal cells in adult virgin mice displayed high levels of ICAM-1, whereas the luminal compartment comprised ICAM1-negative and ICAM1-positive cells (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: ICAM1-positive luminal cells often form cell clusters within the ducts.
source: ICAM1-positive luminal cells, enriched in clonogenic cells, often formed cell clusters within the ducts.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: At early pregnancy, myoepithelial cells lining large ducts strongly express ICAM-1, whereas luminal cells are devoid of ICAM-1.
source: At early pregnancy, myoepithelial cells lining large ducts strongly expressed ICAM-1, whereas luminal cells were devoid of ICAM-1 (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: In developing alveoli and small ducts at early pregnancy, the luminal layer contains clusters of cells positive for ICAM-1.
source: In contrast, in the developing alveoli and small ducts, the luminal layer, presumably enriched in alveolar progenitors, contained clusters of cells positive for ICAM-1 (Figure 9D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 9D.

claim: ER-positive cells are mostly ICAM1-negative.
source: Consistently with qPCR data, ER-positive cells were mostly ICAM1-negative (Figure 9E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 9E.

claim: In adult virgin and early pregnant mice, ICAM-1 expression is restricted to cell–cell contacts.
source: Notably, in adult virgin and early pregnant mice, ICAM-1 expression was restricted to cell–cell contacts, basal-to-basal, basal-to-luminal, and luminal-to-luminal (Figure 9B–E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figures 9B-E.

claim: Icam1-KO females are viable, fertile, and able to feed their pups.
source: The Icam1-KO females are viable, fertile, and able to feed their pups (Xu et al., 1994).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Xu et al., 1994.

claim: Lack of ICAM-1 does not induce visible defects in mammary morphogenesis.
source: Whole-mount analysis of mammary glands from wild-type and Icam1-KO adult virgin and pregnant mice indicated that lack of ICAM-1 did not induce visible defects in mammary morphogenesis (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by whole-mount analysis shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The percentages of basal and luminal cells are not significantly affected in the Icam1-KO epithelium of adult virgin mice.
source: Flow cytometry analysis showed that the percentages of basal and luminal cells were not significantly affected in the Icam1-KO epithelium of adult virgin mice (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Icam1-KO Sca-1-negative luminal cells respond to HGF by increased clonogenicity and production of large spheres.
source: We found that Icam1-KO Sca-1-negative luminal cells responded to HGF by increased clonogenicity and production of large spheres (Figure 9—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: This is supported by sphere culture data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1D and 1E.

claim: In Icam1-KO cells, HGF treatment leads to the induction of basal-specific genes Krt5, Trp63, and Snai2, with a concomitant decrease in Elf5, Gata3, and Hey1.
source: In addition, as previously observed in the presence of ICAM-1, HGF treatment led to the induction of the basal-specific genes Krt5, Trp63, and Snai2, with a concomitant decrease in the regulators of the luminal lineage, Elf5, Gata3, and Hey1 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1F and 1G.

claim: ICAM-1 is not mandatory for mammary development and HGF/Met signaling in luminal progenitors.
source: Thus, ICAM-1 is not mandatory for mammary development and HGF/Met signaling in luminal progenitors.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the Icam1-KO mouse experiments.

claim: ICAM-1 is a new surface marker for the enrichment of mouse mammary luminal progenitors.
source: We report here that ICAM-1 is a new surface marker for the enrichment of mouse mammary luminal progenitors.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data.

claim: Paracrine Met activation stimulates the clonogenic activity of ICAM1-expressing luminal progenitors, controlling their survival and proliferation, and promotes a luminal-to-basal switch while triggering EMT program.
source: We show that paracrine Met activation stimulates the clonogenic activity of ICAM1-expressing luminal progenitors, controlling their survival and proliferation, and promotes a luminal-to-basal switch while triggering EMT program (Figure 10).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data and illustrated in Figure 10.

claim: EMT in luminal progenitors is accompanied by acquisition of regenerative potential, a property restricted to multipotent stem cells.
source: EMT was accompanied by acquisition of regenerative potential, a property restricted to multipotent stem cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the transplantation experiments.

claim: Paracrine HGF signaling can affect the fate of luminal progenitors during mammary development and tumorigenesis.
